data.why: The repo bundles small per-species FASTA files under data/ that are exactly what the file_uploader expects; a primate subset plus a distant outgroup (zebrafish) lets the tree show expected close/distant relationships.

goals: Upload several species' FASTA sequences and generate a k-mer-based distance matrix without sequence alignment
Compare how different distance metrics (Manhattan, Jaccard, Cosine) change the computed distances between the same sequences
Explore how k-mer size (k) affects matrix resolution and resulting tree topology
Generate and inspect a UPGMA dendrogram that visualizes evolutionary relationships among the uploaded species
Export the distance matrix and sequence summary as CSV and the dendrogram as a PNG image for use outside the app

review.summary: The tree describes the app correctly: an alignment-free k-mer, distance matrix and UPGMA tool. Its phases, tasks and cited screens are accurate, and it covers the README's whole workflow, including the metric and k comparisons. Before filing it needs corrections: two feature descriptions disagree with the code (the CSV header mislabels the run if settings change, and the input-check warnings are weaker than f1 claims), two generic Streamlit widgets should be removed as features, and the parameter-guidance panel should be added.
